prompt: Can I take a 20000mAh power bank on a plane, and which one should I get?
queries: airline power bank rules in-flight use ban FAA 2026
answer:
**Yes, you can take a 20000mAh power bank on a plane.**

- **Capacity:** 20000mAh at about 3.7V is roughly 74Wh. That is under the 100Wh limit that most airlines and regulators use, so it needs no special approval.
- **Where to pack it:** Carry-on only. Power banks can't go in checked bags.
- **Airline rules differ on use:** Several airlines now bar you from using or charging a power bank in flight. Examples are [Emirates](https://en.ittefaq.com.bd/13631/emirates-announces-major-change-for-passengers) and [Lufthansa Group](https://business.lufthansagroup.com/am/en/program/experts/news/power-banks-on-board--updated-regulations-from-january-2026). Lufthansa also doesn't allow them in overhead bins. Others are stricter than the baseline too.
- **Number of power banks:** One of the sources I found, [Wego](https://blog.wego.com/new-power-bank-rules-on-flights-in-2026/), reports a limit of two per person. The sources disagree on when that takes effect, so check your airline.
- **U.S. carriers:** I found no FAA-specific rule in my search, so check your airline's policy page before you fly.

**Which one to get**

Most of the model information I found comes from retailer or brand blogs, not independent tests. Treat these as candidates, not tested rankings.

- **[Anker Prime 220W 20100mAh](https://www.anker.com/story/power-banks/best-20000-mah-power-bank):** The best fit if you want to charge a laptop. It's listed at 220W total output and about 72Wh.
- **[Anker 87W 20000mAh](https://www.anker.com/story/power-banks/best-20000-mah-power-bank):** A good all-rounder. It's listed with 87W across three ports and a built-in cable.
- **[INIU Cougar P62-E1](https://iniushop.com/de/blogs/blog/is-20000mah-power-bank-allowed-in-flight):** A cheaper option, listed at 74Wh.
- **Anker Zolo 20000mAh:** A 30W model with a built-in cable. It's enough for a phone or tablet, but I found no Wh rating for it.

Whichever you buy, check that the Wh rating is printed on the case. Security staff and airline crews look for it. If you tell me your budget and what you'll charge, I can narrow this to one pick.
